By Science Correspondent

Some flowers appear to have their own clever way of aiming pollen at bees, according to new research from the University of Vienna.

Scientists have discovered that tiny scoop-shaped structures on some flowers can help shoot pollen towards bees in narrow, fast-moving jets.


The finding could help explain why some plants are particularly good at getting their pollen onto bees.
